messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>

Cc: accounts-payable@novamed.com, trevor.smith@novamed.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Payment cadence and credit ceiling for pilot (NovaMed)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NovaMed is excited to move to a month-long pilot for the GenAssist routing workloads. Before we kick off procurement, finance asked me to surface two things:

1) Can Redwood accommodate a split payment cadence where an initial retainer is paid on contract signature and the remainder billed in two tranches across the pilot (mid and end)?
2) NovaMed prefers Net45 but we may need Net60 for one invoice run in July due to month-end timing. We want to avoid late-fee penalties; is temporary Net60 acceptable for a single invoice?

Also, can we get a short note on what credit cap you would require for the pilot and any evidence your finance team needs (PO, signed SOW, credit application)? I attached a sample PO template.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Procurement — NovaMed Health
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment cadence and credit ceiling for pilot (NovaMed)

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. High level response: yes, we can do a retainer + two tranches structure and we can tolerate a one-off Net60 for July as long as the remaining cadence is Net45 after that. To keep things operationally simple, we usually formalize this as: 25% retainer on signature, 35% mid-pilot invoice (30 days after signature), 40% final invoice (45 days after final invoice). For the single Net60 exception we will bill per normal Net45 terms and provide a one-time pay window extension — no penalties if paid by Net60.

Credit cap: for a month-long pilot at expected consumption the typical unsecured cap we’d provision is $45k. If NovaMed needs higher, we require a short credit application + PO and then Finance will either increase the unsecured cap or ask for a refundable deposit. I attached a draft payment schedule and our standard SLA for reference.

Next steps:
- Jordan will confirm expected monthly consumption so we can set an accurate cap.
- Marissa, could you confirm the internal tilt on approving a $45k unsecured pilot cap vs a deposit?

If that works, I’ll put together a short amendment and a DocuSign for signature.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Payment cadence and credit ceiling for pilot (NovaMed)

Dylan / Jordan —

Finance POV: $45k unsecured for a month-long pilot is reasonable if we have: PO on file + signed SOW + AP contact (accounts-payable@novamed.com) plus net30/45 historical references. If NovaMed insists on a Net60 for a single run, we can accept one-time Net60 as an exception provided they sign an amendment that explicitly allows the extension and confirms no recurring Net60 expectation.

If they want >$45k unsecured, propose the following options for them:
- Option A: Increase to $75k unsecured after a quick credit app (turnaround 48–72 hrs)
- Option B: Keep $45k cap + refundable security deposit equal to requested overage (deposit held until final reconciliation)

Operational note: For the tranche approach, we need invoice milestones and exact base consumption to put amounts into the payment schedule. I put a couple of notes in the attached "Credit-Assessment-Notes.pdf".

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment cadence and credit ceiling for pilot (NovaMed)

Elena —

Quick follow with an explicit proposal based on our internal review:

Proposal (summary):
- Structure: 25% retainer on signature (invoice due Net30), 35% mid-pilot (Invoice 30 days after signature, net45), 40% final (invoice on pilot close, net45).
- One-time Net60 exception: Allowed for the July invoice only (must be marked in amendment).
- Credit cap: $45,000 unsecured by default. If NovaMed needs >$45k, you can either submit a short credit application for up to $75k unsecured (48–72h review) or provide a refundable deposit for the overage.
- Required docs to finalize cap: Signed SOW, PO, AP contact, and the amendment acknowledging the single Net60 exception.

I attached the Proposed_Payment_Schedule_v1.xlsx with milestone rows pre-filled based on our discussion. If you can confirm expected consumption (Jordan — any estimate you want to share here?), we can lock amounts and ship DocuSign.

If acceptable, we will:
1) Send amendment + payment schedule through DocuSign.
2) Finance (Marissa) completes credit check (if you choose Option A) or we confirm deposit instructions.

Cheers,
Dylan
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear proposal — that structure works for us. A few quick clarifications before DocuSign:
- We accept the 25/35/40 tranche split.
- We will need the single Net60 exception for our July run; will sign the amendment to confirm it’s one-off.
- We prefer Option A (credit app) to avoid upfront cash movement; please send the credit application and we will complete it immediately.

Jordan: our consumption estimate for the pilot is ~400k tokens/day peak, ~250k tokens/day average. If that doesn't align with Redwood's baseline, let us know.

Please send the DocuSign and credit app and we will prioritize turnaround.

Regards,
Elena
